title: Implement tenant geo-sticky sessions with KMS usage ledger and RBAC v2 affinity
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds tenant-level geo-sticky session support and an immutable KMS usage ledger. Provides RBAC v2 affinity rules to restrict operator actions by region. Backwards compatible; opt-in via tenant flag.
description: Context: Several enterprise customers requested hardening for data-residency controls that go beyond static region pinning: sessions created by upstream routing gateways can bounce across regions during autoscaling and fail compliance attestations. This PR implements a geo-sticky session model that binds a tenant's short-lived inference session to a residency-aligned region while still allowing failover. It also adds a tamper-evident KMS usage ledger to record which CMKs were used for each session request and which region was authoritative. Goals: 1) provide a tenant opt-in mode (tenant.configuration.geo_sticky=true) that pins sessions to a region for the session lifetime, 2) enforce RBAC v2 affinity so operator/automation roles scoped to other regions cannot act on pinned sessions, 3) emit an immutable ledger entry (signed envelope) on first KMS usage per session for audit and forensic queries, and 4) degrade gracefully with automatic fallback to a pre-authorized region when the preferred region is unavailable. Migration and rollout plan: opt-in per tenant, default off; pilot with 5 tenants in EU while monitoring latency and KMS throttle metrics; add canary gate in routing (10% of traffic) before ramping. Implementation summary: - Routing layer: add geo-sticky cookie/token that includes region claim + ephemeral session nonce; token signed by routing service key and validated by serving runtime. - RBAC: extend rbac-v2 policy language with a new affinity predicate region_affinity == request.session.region that can be evaluated at decision time; new policy templates shipped under security/regional_affinity_templates/*.yaml. - KMS ledger: a new write-once ledger table (ledger.kms_usage) with entries encrypted under a ledger CMK and signed with a ledger attestation key; entries include tenant_id, session_nonce, cmk_id, region, timestamp, request_signature (base64). Ledger entries are written asynchronously but before the first response is returned; fallback writes are queued and retried on transient KMS errors. - Observability: dashboard panels for "geo_sticky.session_pinning_rate", "kms_ledger.write_failures", and policy decision latencies. - Tests: unit tests for region_affinity predicate, ledger envelope signer, and integration test that simulates cross-region failover. Checklist: [x] RFC reviewed with Security and SRE teams, [x] Linear ticket ENG-4271 created, [x] Unit + integration tests added, [x] Console UI change to show tenant geo-sticky flag behind feature toggle, [x] Canary gating and metric alarms configured. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged; RBAC templates provided are additive. Known limitations: session stickiness increases cold-start pressure on the pinned region under certain load patterns; mitigation via autoscaler tuning and routing-batch draining is documented in the runbook. See the commits and files changed for details.
commits: 5 commits: 1) add geo-sticky token middleware and tests; 2) extend rbac-v2 policy evaluator with region_affinity predicate; 3) implement kms_usage ledger writer + signer; 4) add console toggle and tenant migration script; 5) add dashboards and runbook updates.
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: (1) can we make ledgers configurable per-tenant CMK? Some customers want ledger encryption under their CMK. (2) need stronger timeout behavior for ledger writes to avoid blocking the response path.

Maya Chen (author): Response: both addressed. Ledger writer now accepts tenant_cmk_id optional override; if present the writer attempts EncryptWithTenantCMK otherwise falls back to ledger CMK. Ledger write is performed synchronously only for the minimal envelope then the heavy re-encryption and fanout is done async with retries. Added tests for both flows.
Elena Sokolova: Policy evaluator change looks good. Please add unit test coverage for multi-operator scenarios where policy caches might return stale region claims.
Maya Chen: Added cache invalidation hook and tests: policy cache TTL configurable, invalidation on credential rotation and region-change events.
Benji Park: CI flake observed on the signer test due to RNG non-determinism. Recommend seeding or deterministic fixtures.
Maya Chen: Switched to deterministic fixture keys in tests; CI green locally.
ci_checks: integration-tests: initial fail on signer timeout -> re-run -> pass
merge: squash and merge by Arjun Patel. Merge commit includes condensed changelog and Linear reference ENG-4271.
postmerge_tasks: 1) monitor geo_sticky.session_pinning_rate and kms_ledger.write_failures for two weeks, 2) run migration script for pilot tenants, 3) roll out canary gate in routing to 10% after 48h of stable metrics, 4) enable tenant-level tenant_cmk_id only after compliance review.
notes_for_ops: Runbook added at runbooks/geo_sticky_runbook.md. Key operational points: ledger writes are queued in SQS on KMS throttles; retention policy for ledger entries is crypto-managed and requires legal sign-off before purge. If region becomes unavailable, routing will attempt pre-authorized fallback regions based on tenant.residency_policy.fallback_order.
